renderReviewInventoryStatus:204 backfills a missing current-wave lane with the PREVIOUS wave's terminal, so an unsaturated wave displays five 'pass' rows alongside a LANES_INCOMPLETE blocker; this misled the story owner into reporting saturation reached (topology critic F-113)

evaluateReviewInventoryWave (review-inventory-epoch.ts:361) aggregates rawFindings only over epoch.requiredLanes, which excludes lattice-review-topology-critic; the critic's own findings (e.g. F-113, high, open) are therefore invisible to New verified findings and unresolvedFindingIds, so a wave can report saturation while a high-severity critic finding is open. No separate gate requires a valid topology_critic_receipt before review_inventory_finalize either.

pre-review-check.ts:406 raises PR_ARTIFACT_TAMPERED as a four-condition OR whose fourth branch is merely digest(artifact) !== digest(expected), i.e. staleness. A pre-review artifact with an intact signature, intact signer key and correct storyId that has simply gone stale (e.g. after a scope-contract change) is reported as TAMPERED, which reads as a security event and misdirects remediation. Verified on B-3f3d: signature present, signerPublicKey present, storyId correct, artifact untouched since Aug 16 while the scope contract moved Aug 17. Staleness needs a distinct code from tampering.

review_inventory_status renders 'Verified findings: 0' / 'New verified findings: 0' whenever no critic disposition exists yet, because the count at review-inventory-epoch.ts:410 only includes findings the critic already dispositioned as verified_family. On epoch RI-048 this printed zeros while three lanes simultaneously showed status 'finding' (F-114 high, F-115 high, F-116 medium) and zero waves were recorded. The output is technically correct but reads as 'no findings', and this session's owner did misread it as saturation progress. Status should distinguish 'no findings exist' from 'findings exist but are not yet dispositioned'.

CHK-005 declares acceptance path B3F3D-005-H1:VPP-B3F3D-REPLAY-REPORT with producer/consumer endpoints EP-B3F3D-REPLAY-PRODUCER and EP-B3F3D-REPLAY-CONSUMER, but no symbol named runReplayAcceptance exists in packages/main/src (zero grep hits), so acceptance_topology_check reports PR_PLANNED_PATH_UNRESOLVED. The underlying behaviour IS implemented: review-inventory-epoch-smoke.ts:497 defines replay(), invoked twice at lines 639-640 for determinism, covering churn-reduction replay, OPEN-epoch mutation barrier, saturation waves and receipt consumption/replay rejection. The gap is that replay() is a module-local function rather than an exported named acceptance producer matching the declared path. Fix is to export it under the declared name or amend the declaration to the real symbol -- not to write new behaviour.

checklist_get reports 6/6 done for B-3f3d while findings F-118 and F-119 prove CHK-005 and CHK-004 never delivered their declared userSees output. CHK-005 promises five labeled literal lines but review-inventory-epoch-smoke.ts:782 prints JSON and throws an uncaught AssertionError instead of printing FAIL; CHK-004 promises literal strings including 'Remediation authorized once by epoch <id>' and 'This receipt does not authorize TEST' which have zero grep hits anywhere in packages/main/src. Marking an item done performs no mechanical check that its userSees contract is satisfied, so 'all items done' can coexist with unmet delivery promises and reads as completion evidence to an operator. This is the same class of misleading-green signal as BUG-VERIFIED-COUNT-MISREADS-AS-CLEAN and BUG-STATUS-STALE-LANE.

review_inventory epoch writes serialize on a single per-story lock (.lattice/locks/review-inventory/<story>-epochs.lock), so parallel reviewer lanes contend for it on every review_run_start and review_pass_set. Observed on B-3f3d RI-048: quality waited ~7min, test-coverage ~6min, and in wave 2 the docs lane was starved through 45+ consecutive failed attempts (RR-482..RR-533) until the competing writer stopped, nearly losing ~40min of completed review work. Each failed attempt also burns a ReviewRun id. Wait time grows with dispatch parallelism, so the documented parallel-lane workflow degrades exactly as it scales. Contention is worsened by any concurrent status polling, which takes the same lock. Consider finer-grained locking (per-lane rows), a queue with fair ordering, or making review_pass_set retry internally rather than surfacing lock timeout to the caller.

Three separate checklist items on this story declared userSees output that no code path produces: CHK-003 (F-120: promises 'Wave: n/max' and lane states pending|complete|blocked, but review-inventory.ts:258 emits 'Current wave: n/max' and the ReviewInventoryLaneTerminal type at types.ts:1670 is only 'pass'|'finding'), CHK-004 (F-119) and CHK-005 (F-118). All three were marked done and all three passed DEV-to-REVIEW. Each was caught only by a human-style reviewer grepping for the promised literals, and only across three separate waves -- wave 1 caught none, wave 2 caught two, wave 3 caught the third. Nothing in the pipeline compares a userSees string against emitted output, so the field carries the weight of a delivery contract while receiving none of the enforcement. Either mechanically check declared literals against code, or stop presenting userSees as a contract.

currentTopologyReceiptStateForContext (proofstory.ts:309) verifies preReview?.preReviewBasisArtifact ?? planArtifact and throws at line 323 when basisVerification fails, BEFORE either verdict branch, so topology_critic_receipt_set is closed for BOTH pass and request_changes. Preferring the frozen pre-review snapshot is correct security design -- it is captured at pre-review time (pre-review-check.ts:366) so the story owner cannot regenerate their way past the critic. The defect is that once that snapshot goes stale (here: scope-contract changed Aug 17, snapshot dated Aug 16), the only writer that can refresh it is pre_review_check, which is allowedPhases ['DEV'], and DEV requires a finalized review-inventory receipt, which requires a critic terminal state, which is exactly what is blocked. Regenerating the plan basis does not help because line 309 ignores it whenever a pre-review artifact exists. Verified live: topology_critic_receipt_set with verdict=request_changes throws identically to verdict=pass; an independent topology-critic agent reproduced this on its own dispatch. A critic must be able to record request_changes even when the basis it is judging is stale -- refusing a NEGATIVE verdict on stale evidence is what makes the deadlock inescapable.
